title: From systems to cells: Metabolic mechanisms underlying risk divergence in Alzheimer’s disease and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis
title_zh: 从系统到细胞：阿尔茨海默病与肌萎缩侧索硬化症风险差异的代谢机制
abstract: Epidemiological studies show an inverse relationship between metabolic disorders and two major neurodegenerative diseases, Alzheimer's disease (AD) and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS). Obesity, type 2 diabetes (T2DM), and reduced physical activity increase AD risk, whereas in ALS cardiometabolic factors, particularly T2DM, show inverse, age-dependent associations with disease risk. This review integrates epidemiological, clinical, and experimental evidence to suggest that cell-type-specific energy metabolism underlies these contrasting risk profiles. Neurons and skeletal muscle differ in metabolic organization, substrate use, and redox capacity. Neurons rely mainly on glucose and lactate and have limited fatty acid oxidation, making them vulnerable to lipid overload, insulin resistance, and oxidative stress, hallmarks of AD. In contrast, skeletal muscle is metabolically flexible, efficiently oxidizes fatty acids, and has strong antioxidant defenses, which may protect against ALS. These cell-type-specific metabolic profiles are proposed to causally shape disease susceptibility: neuronal lipid overload and impaired redox homeostasis promote amyloid and tau pathology in AD, whereas preserved muscle fatty acid oxidation and antioxidant capacity support neuromuscular junction stability and delay motor neuron degeneration in ALS. Hypermetabolism, hypothalamic dysfunction, glial-neuronal coupling and lactate shuttling may further shape disease susceptibility. Overall, these patterns likely reflect distinct cellular responses to metabolic stress.
abstract_zh: 流行病学研究显示代谢紊乱与两种主要神经退行性疾病——阿尔茨海默病（AD）和肌萎缩侧索硬化症（ALS）之间存在逆向关系。肥胖、2型糖尿病（T2DM）和体力活动减少会增加AD风险，而在ALS中，心血管代谢因素，尤其是T2DM，则呈现与年龄相关的逆向关联。本文综述了流行病学、临床和实验证据，提出细胞类型特异性的能量代谢是导致这些对立风险特征的根本原因。神经元与骨骼肌在代谢组织、底物利用和氧化还原能力上存在差异。神经元主要依赖葡萄糖和乳酸，脂肪酸氧化有限，易受脂质过载、胰岛素抵抗和氧化应激的影响，这些是AD的标志。相反，骨骼肌代谢灵活，能高效氧化脂肪酸，并具备强大的抗氧化防御，可能对ALS具有保护作用。这些细胞特异性的代谢特征被认为可因果地塑造疾病易感性：神经元脂质过载和氧化还原失衡促进AD中的淀粉样蛋白和tau病理；而保持肌肉脂肪酸氧化和抗氧化能力则支持神经肌肉接头的稳定，延缓ALS中的运动神经元退化。高代谢率、下丘脑功能障碍、胶质-神经元耦合以及乳酸转运可能进一步影响疾病易感性。总体而言，这些模式可能反映了细胞对代谢压力的不同响应。
